blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: This paper presents a novel strategy for UAV detection through visible (RGB) and infrared (IR) fusion, in order to improve accuracy and precision in harsh environments and weather conditions. In this research, two opposite approaches have been studied and implemented: the first concerns image-level (early) fusion, which merges two different spectra into a single image to which one detector is applied. On the other hand, the second approach, called decision-level (late) fusion, focuses on blending together the output bounding boxes of two different detection pipelines, aiming to create a common result that can be applied to both spectra simultaneously. Both strategies have been extensively tested in a dedicated environment, which included alternating low and high brightness scenes, different backgrounds (sky and ground), distances (5, 25 and 60 m), altitudes and zoom levels (1X, 2X and 4X). These tests allowed for the assessment of actual detection capabilities and system reliability in real-world applications. Furthermore, the two fusion strategies were evaluated and compared over a set of aligned images in order to highlight the better approach of the two. The results indicate that early fusion achieves better raw performance, since it incorporates the thermal information from the beginning of the training process. However, late fusion presents an innovative and useful detection workflow that can be applied in cases of sensor or frame misalignment. Both positive and negative aspects have also been pointed out and discussed, in order to give a more comprehensive overview. Finally, the paper outlines implementation considerations and practical recommendations based on operational priorities. Overall, the findings contribute to the research in RGB-IR fusion modalities, with the goal of enhancing UAV detection capabilities.
blocks.zh: 本文提出了通过可见(RGB)和红外(IR)聚变进行无人驾驶航空器探测的新策略,以在恶劣环境和天气条件下提高准确度和精确度. 在这项研究中,研究并执行了两种相反的方法: 第一种是图像级(早期)聚变,将两个不同的光谱合并成一个单一的图像,用于一个探测器. 另一方面,第二种方法称为决策级(后期)聚变,其重点是将两个不同探测管的输出边框混合在一起,目的是形成一个共同的结果,可以同时应用于两个光谱. 这两项战略都在一个专门的环境中进行了广泛的测试,其中包括交替的低亮度和高亮度场景,不同的背景(天空和地上),距离(5、25和60米),高度和放大水平(1X、2X和4X)。 这些测试有助于评估实际世界应用中的实际探测能力和系统可靠性。 此外,对两个聚变战略进行了评价并比较了一套一致的图像,以突出两者的更好办法。 结果表明,早期聚变可以实现更好的原始性能,因为它从培训过程一开始就纳入了热能信息。 然而,后聚变呈现出一种创新而有用的检测工作流程,可用于传感器或帧错配的情况. 还提出并讨论了积极和消极两个方面,以便进行更全面的概述。 最后,文件根据业务优先事项概述了执行方面的考虑和切实可行的建议。 总体而言,研究结果有助于RGB-IR聚变方式的研究,目的是提高无人驾驶航空器的探测能力.

blocks.en: I Introduction
blocks.zh: 一. 导言

blocks.en: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are becoming increasingly common in military and civilian applications. They can be used in surveillance, mapping and transporting materials. However, there are safety and security concerns which have to be taken into consideration, since modern UAVs might be able to operate in varied environments and evade traditional surveillance methods. In order to reduce these weaknesses, many advanced sensors are used in current scenarios. For example, visible light (RGB) cameras are widely adopted, as they offer excellent spatial resolutions and reduced costs [ 1 ] . However, they have problems in low light, adverse weather conditions [ 2 ] and crowded backgrounds. Concerning this particular aspect, the terrain texture may be difficult to separate from the drone’s surface, since UAVs are usually made from composite and camouflaged materials. On the other hand, infrared (IR) cameras work effectively in low light situations and night scenes. Nevertheless, they have reduced thermal and spatial resolution and are expensive. Therefore, this research focuses on fused solutions for UAV detection, aiming to combine the strengths of both sensors [ 3 ] . There are some studies in Computer Vision which have explored the capabilities of sensor fusion strategies in object detection systems [ 4 ] . However, the Counter-UAV setting still remains an underexplored research area for fusion. Most of the existing approaches require significant adjustments and fixes to the sensors before fusion can be applied. In this paper, the following innovative fusion pipelines for YOLO-based Counter-UAV detection have been adopted and evaluated: • An image-level (early) fusion that composes synchronized and aligned RGB and IR inputs into a unified representation for a single detector. • A decision-level (late) fusion that processes RGB and IR streams independently and merges their detections post-inference.

blocks.en: This work presents two RGB–IR fusion architectures for drone-to-drone detection using YOLO: an image-level (early) fusion combining synchronized inputs into a single stream, and a decision-level (late) fusion merging outputs from separate detectors. Evaluated across varied conditions, the study compares accuracy, efficiency, and robustness, offering practical guidance for Counter-UAV deployment.

blocks.en: II Related Work
blocks.zh: 二. 相关工作

blocks.en: II-A Detection Techniques
blocks.zh: II-A 探测技术

blocks.en: The detection of small unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) has attracted increasing attention due to their rapid proliferation and the associated security implications [ 5 ] . Early vision-based UAV detection methods relied primarily on classical image processing and handcrafted feature extraction techniques. Background subtraction, motion-based segmentation and orientation detection were commonly employed in static-camera surveillance scenarios, leveraging temporal consistency to isolate moving aerial targets [ 6 ] . Feature-based approaches utilizing Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) [ 7 ] , Haar-like features and Scale-Invariant Feature Transform (SIFT) [ 8 ] descriptors were also explored for detecting aerial objects against sky backgrounds. While computationally efficient, such methods often suffer from limited robustness under dynamic backgrounds, illumination changes and cluttered scenes. The emergence of deep learning has significantly advanced object detection performance [ 9 ] . Two-stage detectors, such as Faster R-CNN [ 10 ] , achieve high detection accuracy through region proposal mechanisms followed by classification and regression refinement. In addition, they offer strong capabilities in feature extraction tasks. However, their computational complexity can limit real-time applicability in resource-constrained operational environments. In contrast, one-stage detectors, including Single Shot MultiBox Detector (SSD) [ 11 ] and the You Only Look Once (YOLO) [ 12 ] family, directly predict bounding boxes and class probabilities in a unified framework, enabling significantly higher inference speeds [ 13 ] . Moreover, models based on transformers, such as Vision Transformers (ViT) [ 14 , 15 ] , DEtection TRansformer (DETR) [ 16 ] and Spatio-Temporal Transformer [ 17 ] , have increased overall robustness by capturing long-range dependencies within images. Furthermore, advanced multimodal deep learning models with hybrid CNN-transformer architectures enhance both feature extraction and decision making through data obtained from numerous sensors. Additionally, the integration of multi-sensor systems into embedded platforms has substantially increased their value in practical applications, including drone surveillance and search-and-rescue operations, demonstrating the effectiveness of these multi-sensor approaches. Recent UAV vision research has also explored multimodal approaches beyond conventional object detection. Lu et al. [ 18 ] proposed MTCNet, a multimodal network for time-sensitive target concealment in UAV aerial imagery, while Tang et al. [ 19 ] introduced R2PLoc, a region-to-point framework for UAV visual geo-localization. These works further demonstrate the increasing adoption of multimodal and hierarchical visual representations in UAV-based perception systems. Classification-and-regression-based detectors, such as YOLO, have become particularly attractive for UAV detection due to their favorable trade-off between accuracy and latency and wide compatibility with many devices. Several studies have adapted YOLO architectures for small-object detection, aerial surveillance and drone monitoring tasks [ 20 ] . Modifications such as multi-scale feature aggregation and anchor box optimization have been proposed to improve sensitivity to small aerial targets. Nevertheless, most existing UAV detection approaches rely solely on visible-spectrum imagery, which inherently limits performance under low-light, night-time or adverse weather conditions [ 21 ] . These limitations motivate the exploration of complementary sensing modalities to enhance robustness in real-world Counter-UAV applications, potentially involving other drones in the detection process [ 22 ] .

blocks.en: II-B Fusion Techniques
blocks.zh: II-B 融合技术

blocks.en: Overall, RGB and infrared modalities exhibit complementary characteristics. Therefore, their integration represents a promising direction for enhancing UAV detection performance in operational Counter-UAV scenarios [ 23 , 24 ] . Methods such as deep fusion networks and attention mechanisms have shown significant improvements in accuracy, particularly in scenarios such as low-visibility conditions and occlusions [ 25 ] , but also in challenging cases such as the resemblance between drones and birds. Furthermore, several studies have shown interest in RGB and IR image fusion methods, with the goal of creating highly informative multi-modal images that integrate features from both spectra. These techniques employ two-scale image decomposition [ 26 ] , contrast enhancement [ 27 ] and swin transformer [ 28 ] . However, they usually need aligned image pairs for achieving fusion, which are not always available due to the sensors’ physical limitations. For this reason, some fusion methods have been developed to also integrate image registration and alignment [ 29 , 30 ] . However, recent works have explored approaches for fusing spatially misaligned yet temporally synchronized images [ 31 ] . Furthermore, multi-modal object detection has already been explored by Yue Cao et al. [ 32 ] and Fan Xu et al. [ 33 ] . More recently, Zhang et al. proposed CCSFuse [ 34 ] , a collaborative compensation and selective fusion framework specifically designed for UAV-based RGB-IR object detection, further demonstrating the growing interest in feature-level fusion for multimodal aerial detection. Some studies also involve Bayesian fusion for enhancing perception [ 35 ] . Some studies also involve Bayesian fusion for enhancing perception [ 35 ] . Modern approaches also integrate additional data sources such as LiDAR and radar, in order to enhance depth perception and robustness, although these methods are mainly oriented toward pedestrian detection [ 36 ] . In the UAV domain, RGB-T fusion detectors such as SF-YOLO [ 37 ] have also been proposed for drone scenes. Nevertheless, despite these recent advances, publicly available UAV detection methods operating on multimodal fused data remain comparatively limited, particularly when considering practical constraints such as sensor misalignment and real-time deployment. After this brief introduction, in the following subsections we delve deeper into the three most important fusion methods families: early-fusion, mid-fusion and late-fusion.
blocks.zh: 总体而言,RGB和红外线模式显示出互补特点。 因此,将它们整合起来,是提高无人驾驶飞行器在反无人驾驶飞行器作业情景中探测性能的一个有希望的方向[23、24]。 深度聚变网络和关注机制等方法在准确性方面显示出显著改善,特别是在低可见度条件和隐蔽性[25]等情景中,但在无人机和鸟类的相似性等具有挑战性的情况中尤为如此. 此外,一些研究显示对RGB和IR图像聚变方法感兴趣,目的是创建信息丰富的多模式图像,将两个光谱的特性结合起来。 这些技术采用两级图像分解[26],对比增强[27]和swin变压器[28]. 然而,它们通常需要配对的图像对来实现核聚变,由于传感器的物理限制,这些图像对并非总能得到. 为此,还开发了一些聚变方法,以整合图像注册和对齐[29,30]. 然而,最近的工作探索了在空间上错位但时间同步的图像的引信方法[31]。 此外,Yue Cao等人[32]和Fan Xu等人已经探索过多式物体探测。 [33]. 近来, 张等人提出CCSFuse[34],这是专门为UAV型RGB-IR天体探测而设计的协同补偿和选择性聚变框架,进一步表明对多模式航空探测的特征级聚变的兴趣越来越大. 一些研究还涉及巴伊西亚聚变,以提高知觉[35]. 一些研究还涉及巴伊西亚聚变,以提高知觉[35]. 现代方法还整合了更多数据来源,如LiDAR和雷达,以提高深度感知和坚固度,尽管这些方法主要面向行人探测[36]. 在无人机领域,RGB-T聚变探测器如SF-YOLO[37]也被提议用于无人机场景. 然而,尽管最近取得了这些进展,在多式引信数据上公开使用的无人驾驶航空器探测方法仍然相对有限,特别是在考虑传感器错配和实时部署等实际制约因素时。 在这简短的介绍之后,在以下小节中,我们更深入地探索三种最重要的聚变方法家族:早聚变,中聚变和晚聚变.

blocks.en: II-B 1 Early-Fusion (Pixel-Level)
blocks.zh: II-B 1 早期融合(像素级)

blocks.en:
It combines the information of the two modalities at the pixel level. It is the most intuitive fusion approach, where IR and RGB images are concatenated to generate a 4-channel image, which is then fed into a regular object detection architecture. Several image-level fusion networks have been proposed in the literature, ranging from autoencoder-based methods such as DenseFuse [ 38 ] to illumination-aware architectures such as PIAFusion [ 39 ] , IAIFNet [ 40 ] and FCDFusion [ 41 ] . These techniques rely on dedicated, relatively complex fusion architectures to better merge the images in the two spectra. However, as Wagner et al. show [ 42 ] , pixel-level fusion was outperformed by deeper fusion variants in their pedestrian detection experiments, even though there are ways to improve it, such as the ones presented by Tianyi Zhao et al. [ 43 ] .
Since aligned RGB-Thermal datasets are not available, the method developed by Lizhi Yang et al. [ 44 ] has also been evaluated, which uses a CycleGAN to create aligned synthetic RGB/IR data [ 45 , 46 ] . In fact, it is important that the image pairs are perfectly aligned before performing early-fusion. In a more simplified way, this architecture can be described as a neural network composed of two different branches, dedicated respectively to RGB and IR image processing. In addition, this network presents a decision layer, which chooses how much importance to give to which of the two sub-networks. In order to merge RGB and IR images, it is possible to use Python Imaging Library (PIL or Pillow) or dstack. The approach that these two techniques follow is based on the raw channel information overlapping. In fact, they take into consideration the bit depth of RGB images, which refers to the number of bits used to represent the color of a single pixel. It is usually 24 bits (8 bits for each color channel) plus other 8 bits for transparency (alpha channel). However, the transparency channel is not always present and it depends on the extension in which the image file is saved. In fact, if more than 3 channels are needed, the .png format needs to be considered, since .jpg supports a maximum of 3 channels. For IR images, only their thermal information (8 bits) should be considered, which will be added to the final fused image. Therefore, the resulting merged image will be of 32 bits.

blocks.en: II-B 2 Late-Fusion (Decision-Level)
blocks.zh: II-B 2 晚会(决定级)

blocks.en: This fusion type merges detection results from separate models, improving robustness by leveraging complementary sensor characteristics. Furthermore, the aligned inputs (RGB and the respective IR counterpart) of the two modalities are fed separately into two unimodal object detection models to generate bounding boxes and the predicted boxes are fused using statistical methods, such as weighted averaging of the bounding box coordinates, which is based on the confidence scores from each modality. This method gives more importance to the bounding boxes with higher confidence scores, and this is a suitable option for the purpose of UAV detection. This method works with both aligned and misaligned images. For this reason, it could be considered more resilient to sensor misalignment with respect to early fusion. However, when the same object appears with different orientations or in different positions across the two images, the resulting bounding boxes may be less precise in terms of localization. In practice, the bounding box tends to expand, and especially in the case of unaligned images, the object is still correctly identified while the box remains largely consistent across both views. As a result, the final bounding box may show slight variations in size and position. In addition to the adopted strategy, there exist also ensemble methods such as probabilistic ensembling [ 35 ] , in which a bounding box is considered valid if it is detected by both modalities.
blocks.zh: 这种聚变类型融合了不同模型的检测结果,通过利用互补的传感器特性提高了强度. 此外,两种模式的对齐输入(RGB和相应的IR对应方)被分别输入两个单模式对象检测模型,以生成边框,而预测的框则采用统计方法进行组合,如边框坐标加权平均值,这种组合基于每种模式的置信分数。 这种方法更重视置信分数较高的边框,对于无人机探测目的来说,这是一个合适的选择. 这种方法与对齐和错配的图像同时起作用. 因此,可以认为它对传感器在早期聚变方面的错配具有更强的复原力。 然而,当同一物体在两个图像之间出现不同方向或不同位置时,产生的边框在本地化方面可能不太精确. 在实际操作中,边框往往会膨胀,特别是在不相通的图像中,物体仍然被正确识别,而盒子在两种观点之间基本一致. 因此,最终的边框可能显示大小和位置略有变化. 除了所采用的战略外,还存在各种组合方法,如概率组合[35],如果两种模式都检测到一个边框,则认为其有效。

blocks.en: II-B 3 Mid-Fusion (Feature-Level)
blocks.zh: II-B 3 中间融合(一级)

blocks.en: This strategy, which falls between early and late fusion techniques [ 47 ] , might be the best and most balanced option to choose when trying to develop a computer vision system that exploits sensor fusion. Essentially, this fusion integrates feature maps extracted separately from RGB and IR modalities before applying detection networks. More specifically, features are captured from each of the two spectra using specific convolutional pipelines in the first stages. Subsequently, feature maps are merged using methods like concatenation or sum, which prepare information to be used for the final layers of detection. Taking into account these aspects, the mid-fusion idea has the ability to improve the robustness of computer vision and object detection systems in harsh environments with low light [ 48 , 49 ] . This type of fusion has also many advantages compared with the other two. First of all, images do not need to be merged into a single one as early-fusion does, but all their channels are kept in the original form, preserving modality-specific information. Nor are the final detection results combined using statistical methods. Therefore, this strategy appears to be more flexible with respect to the input data type and the final detection goals that we may have. In fact, it has already been studied and implemented in some feature alignment methods for RGB and IR images [ 50 ] . Recent UAV-specific work further supports this direction. Zhang et al. [ 34 ] proposed CCSFuse, which performs collaborative compensation and selective fusion for RGB-IR object detection, illustrating how modality-specific features can be selectively combined to improve multimodal UAV perception. However, despite these positive aspects, only the other two strategies have been implemented, as mid-fusion implies creating a custom detection architecture, markedly different from the state-of-the-art YOLO one used for the tests. In addition, early-fusion and late-fusion allowed us to obtain useful metrics for comparing the strategies in several scenarios, which were not possible with mid-fusion.
blocks.zh: 这一策略介于早期和晚期聚变技术[47]之间,在试图开发利用传感器聚变的计算机视觉系统时,可能是最佳和最平衡的选择. 基本上,这种聚变结合了在应用检测网络之前从RGB和IR模式中分离出来的特征图. 更具体地说,从两个光谱的每个光谱中,在第一阶段使用特定的演化管道捕捉特征. 随后,地物图使用凝聚或和等方法进行合并,这些方法准备用于最终检测层的信息. 考虑到这些方面,中聚变想法具有在低光度的恶劣环境中提高计算机视觉和物体探测系统的稳健性[48,49]. 与其他两种核聚变相比,这种核聚变也有诸多优点. 首先,图像不需要像早期聚变那样合并成一个单一的,但是其所有通道都以原始形式保存,保存模式特定信息. 最后的检测结果也没有采用统计方法加以合并。 因此,在输入数据类型和我们可能拥有的最后检测目标方面,这项战略似乎更加灵活。 事实上,它已经在RGB和IR图像的一些特征对齐方法中得到了研究和实施[50]. 最近针对无人驾驶航空器的工作进一步支持这一方向。 张等. [34] 建议的CCSFuse,它为RGB-IR对象检测进行协作补偿和选择性聚变,说明如何有选择地将特定模式的特征结合起来,以改善多式联运无人驾驶航空器的感知. 然而,尽管有这些积极方面,但只有另外两项战略得到执行,因为中化意味着建立一个定制检测架构,这与用于测试的最先进的YOLO架构明显不同。 此外,早期核聚变和晚期核聚变使我们能够获得有用的衡量标准,用于在几种情况下对战略进行比较,而这与中期核聚变是不可能的。

blocks.en: III Logical Proposed Architectures
blocks.zh: 三、拟议逻辑结构

blocks.en: The architecture proposed is based on the YOLO framework, since it represents the state-of-the-art in the real-time object detection field. Moreover, two separate fusion pipelines have been developed for enhancing detection performance and accuracy. Finally, a multimodal dataset [ 51 ] of real-world data on still and moving drones was built, for testing the validity of the following fusion methods. This approach has been preferred to the synthetic one because real acquired data better reflect operational conditions and lead to superior performance. In addition, the actual behaviour of a drone, that is, its ability to rotate, shift and change pose over the three axes (roll, pitch and yaw), has also been considered while collecting data. The paired dataset comprises 400 aligned images (300 for training and 100 for validation, following a 75/25 split) for each fusion strategy evaluated, starting from a base of aligned RGB-IR pairs.
blocks.zh: 拟议的架构以YOLO框架为基础,因为它代表了实时对象检测领域的最先进水平. 此外,还开发了两条单独的聚变管道,以提高探测性能和准确性。 最后,建立了一个关于静态和移动无人机的真实世界数据的多式联运数据集[51],以测试下列聚变方法的有效性。 这种方法比合成方法更受青睐,因为实际获得的数据更好地反映了操作条件,并导致更好的性能。 此外,在收集数据时,还考虑了无人机的实际行为,即其旋转、转动和变化能力对三轴(滚子、投子和yaw)的影响。 配对数据集由400个配对图像组成(300个用于培训,100个用于验证,在75/25分拆后),用于评价每个聚变战略,从一个配对RGB-IR配对的基础开始.

blocks.en: III-A Early Fusion
blocks.zh: 三、A 早期融合

blocks.en: The early fusion approach combines RGB and IR images at the pixel level to create a single multimodal input. This approach requires frames to be aligned. This process was performed by applying transformation steps to each image, such as interpolation, perspective distortion and rotation. After this, an overlap of the channels was performed, while removing the transparency level (also called ”A” in RGBA image format), which was present in .png images. However, since the focus of this research strictly concerns the analysis of fusion strategies, the reader is referred to the paper on autonomous UAV detection architecture development [ 52 ] , in which all alignment steps are described. Once spatial alignment between RGB and infrared frames was achieved, the fusion was performed through overlap, by stacking the image channels into a single array of 4 spectra. The RGB image was split into three channels: Red, Green and Blue. Each of them is represented by a two-dimensional intensity map, where every pixel contains intensity values for that particular channel. A visual interpretation is shown in Figure 1 .
blocks.zh: 早期的聚变方法结合了像素级的RGB和IR图像,以创建单一的多式联运输入. 这种办法要求调整框架。 这一过程是通过对每个图像应用转换步骤来实现的,如插图,视角扭曲和旋转. 之后进行了频道的重叠,同时取消了在.png图像中存在的透明级别(RGBA图像格式中也称作"A"). 然而,由于这一研究的重点严格涉及核聚变策略的分析,读者参考了自主无人机探测架构开发论文[52],其中描述了所有对齐步骤. 一旦实现RGB和红外线帧的空间对齐,聚变就通过重叠进行,将图像通道堆叠成一个由4个光谱组成的单数组. RGB图像被分为三个频道: 红绿蓝. 每个都由二维强度图代表,每个像素都包含该特定通道的强度值. 图1显示了视觉解释。

However, Ultralytics introduced support for multi-channel training only recently [ 53 ] , subsequent to the experiments reported here. Hence, although OpenCV2 library, commonly used within YOLO pipelines, allows image loading with an arbitrary number of channels using the cv2.IMREAD_UNCHANGED flag, in previous versions of Ultralytics, in order to use 4-channel inputs, extensive modifications to the YOLO architecture would be required, including adaptation of the model’s input layer and associated preprocessing routines.

Instead, the characteristics of RGB channels were taken into consideration. RGB usually exhibits a high degree of spectral correlation, since most objects in the environment reflect light similarly across the visible spectrum. blocks.en: While the standard RGB configuration achieved higher precision, the overall detection performance did not uniformly surpass the fused models across all evaluation metrics. In fact, the superiority of the three proposed fusion strategies first emerges on mAP@50-95. The highest one is reached by RGT with 56.2%. A similar improvement can be observed on mAP@50, where the proposed fused approach achieves a result of 97.8%, compared to 89.8% of Infrared. These are indexes of good model performance, since mAP evaluates it over all confidence thresholds, rather than at a single operating point. Another important point regards F1-Score, which penalizes models with unbalanced precision and recall values. All these results highlight the improvements of RGT fusion in comparison to the other strategies reported. In fact, the metrics suggest that the proposed multimodal approach has gained the capability to enrich the scope and improve the stability of the model in object detection tasks. In addition, the comparison between fusion strategies enriches the study, highlighting the importance of a dedicated fusion approach with respect to the use-case scenario. Another interesting point regards the results obtained from literature fusion strategies. All of them cannot be considered for real-time purposes, since they rely on dedicated fusion networks (illumination-aware or autoencoder-based) whose computational cost is unsuitable for real-time processing. Thus, even though the FCD approach gives promising results, it is not usable in real-time scenarios. According to the results obtained, the RGT fusion strategy was also better than the other two presented (RBT and GBT). For this reason, it was selected for tests in real-world scenarios. Nevertheless, it should be pointed out that this is a preliminary evaluation step for the topic. It could surely be enriched and extended with a larger fused dataset and other object detection models, in order to carry on the research in the field. A further consideration can be made by comparing the proposed RGT strategy with FCDFusion, which turned to be the two best models. Although FCDFusion outperforms RGT in precision and mAP@50-95, RGT achieves higher recall and mAP@50, while both methods obtain the same F1-Score of 95.2%, indicating comparable overall detection performance. Therefore, the superiority of RGT should not be interpreted exclusively in terms of individual detection metrics, but rather considering the relationship between performance and computational complexity. In fact, FCDFusion requires a dedicated fusion network to generate the fused representation, introducing an additional deep learning model into the processing pipeline. This results in additional computational requirements and increases the overall complexity of the system. Conversely, RGT performs the fusion directly at the frame level, without requiring a dedicated fusion network during inference. The multimodal information can therefore be combined in real time and directly provided to the object detector, which represents a significant advantage for real-world applications.

blocks.en: In the late fusion approach aligned RGB and IR images are processed separately by two object detection models. The resulting bounding boxes are then fused using a weighted average method. For each pair of boxes, the center coordinates are averaged based on their confidence scores, while the maximum width and height are kept to avoid box shrinking. A distance threshold δ \delta is used to decide whether two boxes should be fused. In particular, if the centers of two boxes are within this range, they are fused, otherwise they are left as they are. More in detail, the Euclidean distance between the center points of two bounding boxes in the two spectra is computed. If this distance falls in the threshold set, weighted average is performed. Otherwise, the original box created by the model is preserved. This approach has been designed to avoid discarding detections that may only exist in one modality and to work in case of misaligned frames. In fact, if the centers of the two bounding boxes are near, the system fuses them. Alternatively, it preserves what each model has decided during detection. In the decision-level fusion strategy, two spatially aligned images, one RGB and its corresponding infrared (IR) counterpart, are processed independently by their respective detection models. Each detector produces a set of bounding boxes with associated confidence scores. Fusion is subsequently performed at the bounding box level using a weighted averaging method.

blocks.en: The weighted average approach computes the fused bounding box coordinates based on the confidence scores of the individual detections. This method can be applied to both perfectly aligned and moderately misaligned image pairs. However, if the same object appears with slight positional or orientational discrepancies across the two modalities, the resulting fused bounding box may exhibit reduced localization precision. In such cases, the fused bounding box may become enlarged, encompassing the object regions identified in both modalities within a single unified box. The fusion procedure begins with the computation of the center coordinates of the new bounding box using confidence-weighted averaging. The width and height of the fused bounding box are then defined as the maximum of the corresponding dimensions from the RGB and IR detections. This design choice prevents the fused bounding box from shrinking excessively and ensures that the spatial extent of the detected object is fully preserved. A dedicated fusion function was implemented to manage all detection scenarios. Since decision-level fusion requires detections from both modalities, situations may arise in which a UAV is detected by only one of the two models. In such cases, the bounding boxes generated by the detecting model are retained without modification.

In order to regulate the correspondence between detections from the two modalities, a fixed distance threshold ( δ = 50 \delta=50 pixels) was introduced. This threshold is defined as a geometric correspondence tolerance for the spatial displacement that may occur between RGB and IR detections. Since the two optical axes are physically separated and therefore non-coaxial, the same UAV may appear at different image coordinates in the two modalities due to parallax and residual registration errors. The threshold consequently represents the maximum positional discrepancy considered compatible with the hypothesis that two detections correspond to the same physical target. A fixed pixel-domain threshold was adopted because the proposed fusion operates directly on detector outputs at a fixed input resolution of 640 × 640 640\times 640 pixels. The value of δ \delta is therefore treated as a predefined correspondence tolerance rather than as an optimized detection hyperparameter, and is kept constant throughout the evaluation. In particular, the use of a distance tolerance allows the proposed method to tolerate spatial discrepancies between the two modalities while preventing detections with larger spatial separation from being merged. For each pair of RGB and IR bounding boxes, the Euclidean distance between their center coordinates has also been computed. If this distance is below the threshold, weighted averaging is applied. Otherwise, the bounding boxes are preserved independently. This strategy enables the method to operate effectively under moderate sensor misalignment. When detections are spatially consistent across modalities, fusion is performed; when they differ significantly, each model’s decision is maintained. blocks.en: Different lighting scenarios were faced during the experiments. For safety reasons, a maximum distance of 60 meters and an altitude of 20 m were set for all the tests. Zooming in was also used in borderline cases, where the background was wooded and the drone was camouflaged among the leaves, thus difficult to detect. Confidence scores were increasing when zooming in and the drone was still detected with all degrees of zoom and at great distances. However, detection at 1X is sometimes intermittent, whereas 2X and 4X work reliably, making the system more stable. Furthermore, the score drops when the target flies in front of an obstacle. At those hours, temperatures were lower, which prevented disturbances from light and heat. On the other hand, the sky background greatly improved the confidence score, even with clouds. In fact, the cloud formation let light pass through and the environment was at least sufficiently illuminated, enhancing the contrast between the target UAV and the sky color. Late-fusion technique was more challenging due to the management of two independent models. As can be seen, the stream was aligned during detection, in order to have both frames in the same plane with a horizontal sync. This method proves particularly useful in environments in which one of the two modalities is less reliable. In fact, the best of the two helps the other to perform detection, thanks to the weighted average strategy developed. As before, sky offers higher confidence scores, due to the better contrast between the UAV and the background. However, some small issues have been discovered with trees and terrain setup, as they generate clutter, a phenomenon that challenges the optical sensors. In addition, leaves make detection even more difficult due to the openings inside the trees, which let light in, reducing the possibility of detection. Moreover, since we recorded on summer days, the heat and brightness affected the infrared sensors, generating noise. Another aspect which should be taken into consideration regards UAV movements. If the drone is stationary or changes direction quickly, it can be lost. However, if the drone is in the air, it is much better identified, even at great distances.
blocks.zh: 在试验期间,出现了不同的照明方案。 出于安全考虑,所有试验的最大距离为60米,高度为20米。 在边缘情况下也使用了放大法,背景是木制的,无人机在叶子中被伪装,因此很难发现. 当放大时,信心得分正在增加,无人机仍然以各种程度的放大和远距离探测。 然而,1X的检测有时是断断续续的,而2X和4X的工作是可靠的,使系统更加稳定. 此外,当目标在障碍物面前飞行时,得分下降。 在那些时候,温度较低,从而防止了光和热的扰动。 另一方面,天空背景大大提高了信心分数,即使有云. 事实上,云层的形成让光通过,环境至少被充分照亮,加强了目标无人机与天空颜色之间的对比. 由于对两个独立模型的管理,晚聚技术更具挑战性。 可以看出,该流在探测时被对齐,以便两个帧都在同一平面上进行水平同步. 事实证明,这种方法在两种模式之一不太可靠的环境中特别有用。 事实上,由于制定了加权平均战略,两者中最好的帮助对方进行检测。 和以前一样,由于无人机与背景对比较好,天空提供了更高的信心分数. 然而,随着树木和地形的布局,发现了一些小问题,因为它们产生杂乱无章的现象,对光学传感器构成挑战。 此外,由于树木内部的开口,叶子使检测更加困难,使光线进入,减少了检测的可能性. 此外,自从我们记录到夏天的日子,热和亮度影响了红外线传感器,产生噪音. 关于无人驾驶航空器的运动,应考虑另一个方面。 如果无人机是静止的或者快速改变方向,它可能会丢失. 然而,如果无人机在空中,即使距离遥远,也更能识别.

blocks.en: VI Conclusion and Future Work
blocks.zh: 六. 结论和今后的工作

blocks.en: It has been quite difficult to identify the best strategy of the two fusion techniques. In fact, both early and late fusions gave promising outputs. However, they could be exploited in different contexts. For example, late fusion might be advantageous at night, when the RGB counterpart is completely lost, whereas IR offers better performance and could support it. On the other hand, early fusion is the best for general use, as it improves detection by adopting channel blending, considering the tests conducted and the results acquired. Despite this advantage, early fusion is harder to implement and run, due to the need to train a dedicated model over a fused dataset and its dependence on an accurate pre-alignment process. Although the system reached good overall results, both mathematically and empirically, the need for more multimodal data for future research remains crucial. In particular, the proposed solution was specifically designed for drone-to-drone detection architectures. For this reason, it is necessary to integrate this work with more data, in order to adapt this strategy to different detection pipelines. Some future improvements to the project will surely involve an upgrade to the drone platform, enabling the use of newer and more accurate sensors for detection. This is indeed linked to the exploitation of different and complex image types, such as multispectral or hyperspectral images. However, the use of other sensor data should also be taken into consideration, since radar platforms are widely used for developing sensor fusion paradigms in modern aviation.
blocks.zh: 很难确定两种聚变技术的最佳策略。 事实上,早期和晚期的核聚变提供了有希望的产出。 但是,它们可以在不同的情况下加以利用。 例如,晚聚变在夜间可能有利,因为RGB对应方完全丢失,而IR则提供更好的性能并可以支持它. 另一方面,早期聚变是最好的一般用途,因为它通过采用通道混合,考虑到所进行的试验和获得的结果,改善了检测。 尽管有这一优势,早期核聚变更难实施和运行,因为需要在一个已安装的数据集上训练专用模型,并依赖于准确的预配定过程. 虽然该系统在数学和经验两方面都取得了良好的总体成果,但今后研究需要更多的多式联运数据仍然至关重要。 特别是,拟议的解决方案是专门为无人机对德龙探测架构设计的. 因此,有必要将这项工作与更多的数据结合起来,以便使这一战略适应不同的探测管道。 今后对该项目的一些改进将必然涉及对无人机平台的升级,从而能够使用更新和更准确的传感器进行探测。 这确实与利用不同和复杂的图像类型有关,例如多光谱或超光谱图像。 然而,还应考虑使用其他传感器数据,因为雷达平台被广泛用于发展现代航空中的传感器聚变范式.
